result.summary: The page is largely well-composed and readable. No critical or major breakage found; a few minor cosmetic/consistency issues stand out: the favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently between cards, the search placeholder text is very low contrast, and the active 'Pizza' filter does not appear to be reflected in the restaurant results shown.

issues.description: In the 'Popular right now' list, the heart/favorite icon on the first card (Tokumaru Ramen Bar) is rendered as a bare white outline, while the second card's heart sits inside a dark translucent circular button. The two affordances look like different components.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same circular scrim/background treatment to the favorite button on every card so the control is consistent and remains legible over light imagery.

issues.description: The search field placeholder 'Restaurants, dishes, groceries' is a very light gray on a light gray fill, giving low contrast that may fail WCAG 1.4.3 for users with low vision.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder text (or lighten the field fill) to reach at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the input background.

issues.description: The 'Pizza' category chip is shown as selected, yet the visible results (Green Bowl Poké, Smash Bros Burgers, Tokumaru Ramen Bar) are not pizza places, which makes the filter appear non-functional or confusing.
issues.suggestion: Either filter the carousels to match the selected category, or visually separate global sections (e.g., label them 'Recommended regardless of filter') so the selected chip state is not misleading.

issues.description: The 'Fastest near you' thumbnails use flat, emoji-like illustrations on heavily blurred backgrounds, while 'Popular right now' uses richer full-bleed illustrations; the mixed asset quality makes the top row look like placeholder imagery.
issues.suggestion: Use consistent, production-quality imagery (or a unified illustration style) across both carousels, and avoid blurred backdrops behind small thumbnails.
